extracted.subtask_description: A historical newspaper page (World War II era) reporting government policies, wartime production statistics, administrative Q&A, and civil-defense guidance. Contains descriptions of rules, exemptions, and operational guidance from federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-raid warden recruitment composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A call for replacement of air raid wardens lost to military service and industry — 'at least 50 per cent should be women.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sent by Civilian Defense Director Joseph M. Loughlin: new wardens should include women who should number at least 50 per cent of the wardens organization. New wardens are replacements for those lost to military service or industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air-raid warden training content and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Wardens must be instructed as replacements and given knowledge of other major phases of civilian defense, including the civilian war service program; use of block plan organization for complete coverage of every house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loughlin said re-establishment of a state-wide school system for war-control and competitive programs in recruiting, training and drilling. Training should include a general description of wartime transportation problems, the function, equipment and other details of state and local transportation programs, and the purposes, methods and agencies of control of emergency traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'normal' (customary) bonus
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'normal' bonus is one that an employer has given customarily in the past, e.g., bonuses of a week's or several weeks' pay regularly paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q&A: If corporations regularly give bonuses (one, two or three weeks' pay), that is a normal bonus. Even if paid in good years and not in bad years, assuming it is a good year it is still a customary bonus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary/stabilization coverage and limits (interpretation guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (War Labor Board, Treasury) working on regulations: board has jurisdiction over adjustment of all wages and over adjustment of salaries up to $5,000 a year except executives, administrative and professional employees; separate discussion of a $25,000 net income limit applied elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q&A with Assistant Secretary of the Treasury John L. Sullivan: professional fees are unlimited; a professional in business for himself who from fees gets income considerably in excess of $25,000 is not covered by the act, but if the professional works for a single concern and devotes all his time to that concern he is covered. In the case of an actor working for several companies whose total salary exceeds the limit, all employers will be regarded as participating in the violation. State and municipal employees are 'subject to the regulations' though statutory exceptions may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper production freeze criterion (U.S.-Canadian order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers of paper (newsprint, book and magazine papers included) are forbidden to produce more than their average rate of output in the six months ended September 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The War Production Board and the Wartime Prices and Trade Board (Ottawa) issued parallel orders freezing production at six-month average rates as a preliminary step toward curtailment. Authorities warned further curtailment could reduce production below demand and eat into stocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper product exemptions from restriction order
rubrics_metrics.description: Six paper products were specifically exempted from the restriction order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempted products: building papers, building boards, vulcanizing fiber stock, resin impregnating stock used in plastics, sanitary napkins, and hospital wadding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and delivery restraint for paper/newsprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint orders already forbid a manufacturer to deliver to a consumer, or a consumer to accept, a shipment which would boost his inventory above a set days' supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The orders set limitations to regulate inventories (e.g., to handle milk in metropolitan milksheds and newsprint inventories). The government stated it was 'buying the short-wave broadcast time' and working to coordinate supply and distribution; similar inventory-regulating measures will be taken for paper/newsprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA ceiling on building and repair service sales (scope and filing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Price ceilings over all building and repair service-sales will be set using prices in existence last March; the ceiling applies to jobs that call for equipment or materials plus labor, but will not cover cases where only labor is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPA plans to set specialized ceilings on a by-the-job basis with slight variations to allow for differences. All contracts over $50 must be filed with OPA within ten days after being awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government leasing of short-wave stations (rationale and operating terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government leased ten short-wave broadcasting stations for the duration of the war to transmit OWI programs internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two reasons given: (1) materially improve reception of United States short-wave broadcasts globally, increasing audience; (2) improve the coordination and quality of news and other broadcasts for international consumption. Leases negotiated with broadcasters; broadcasters continue to operate facilities 'without profit' and the Government pays the cost of operations (effectively buying broadcast time).

rubrics_metrics.name: WPB production reporting categories and benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: War Production Board reports measure production in major armament categories (warplanes, ordnance, merchant ships, naval and army vessels) and report month-to-month percentage changes and comparisons to forecast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example measures: airplanes up 10% month-to-month, ordnance up 7%, merchant ship construction measured by value and tonnage (gains reported as percent increases and compared to forecasts). WPB uses 'on schedule' to describe meeting planned production (e.g., four-engined bomber output 'very nearly on schedule').

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles proposed for national manpower planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal for a conference to integrate procurement, production and manpower and resources under a unified directing and planning body; preference expressed for voluntary agreements rather than compulsory national service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labor leaders opposed compulsory drafting and job freezing, advocating a volunteer system of meeting labor needs; the suggested 'conference committee of the nation' would plan machinery for integration of procurement, production and manpower under unified direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police training standard (FBI National Police Academy model)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FBI National Police Academy offers an intensive fourteen-week course similar to that given FBI agents; graduates are expected to have duties as difficult and dangerous as armed forces personnel protecting the home front.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks at graduation emphasized duty 'to protect the home front' and that the N.P.A. was founded to provide intensive training; the course is presented as a model for state and local police training.
